items.summary: Security disposition: evidence_needed for fleet-wide clearance; blocked for public exposure and security-sensitive releases; conditional for ordinary reversible growth. Concrete evidence: fleet-doctor has no run or results; operations deploy, uptime, and error sweeps have no results; authentication boundaries, least privilege, secrets handling, container isolation, release approvals and provenance, dependency and supply-chain controls, data exposure, monitoring, incident response, TLS coverage, and security.txt/disclosure readiness remain unverified. TLS reports no certificates expiring within 30 days, but this does not establish complete TLS posture. Compliance is a technical baseline only: 37 pass, 16 fail, 6 unknown. Retained worker and reviewer failures are containment signals, not evidence of compromise. Risk severity is high for public exposure and security-sensitive release, medium for bounded reversible growth. Exact decision: continue bounded read-only evidence capture, maintain private launch gates, and permit only reversible growth that preserves existing consent, disclosures, data handling, claims, and access boundaries. Do not retrieve credentials, access private containers, exploit targets, change permissions, deploy, add dependencies, expand data collection, requeue failures, or conduct external outreach.

Continue the existing bounded read-only security evidence matrix and failed-work containment only. Record dated evidence, owners, affected scope, explicit unknowns, severity, and release implications for access boundaries, secrets, runtime isolation, build and deployment provenance, dependency controls, TLS, data flows, monitoring, incident readiness, and disclosure readiness. Do not create duplicate telemetry requests or new production work.
